newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU has no comment on Swedish EMU decision.
newsitem.headline: EU has no comment on Swedish EMU decision.

text.p: The European Commission on Tuesday declined comment on Swedish Prime Minister Goran Persson's announcement that his country would not join economic and monetary union (EMU) from the start in 1999.

The spokesman for Commission President Jacques Santer said the Swedish move was a recommendation to a party congress of the ruling Social Democrats in September and was not yet the country's official position.
"This is not the position of Sweden so we will not react to that," spokesman Nicolaus van der Pas told Reuters. "We have no official position we can react to."
The decision not to join in 1999 was taken by the executive committee of the Social Democratic Party. It is expected to be confirmed by the party congress in September and later by parliament.
Van der Pas also referred to the EU's Maastricht treaty which lays down the procedure and timetable for EMU. "And those will be followed," he said.
Under the 1992 treaty, all countries which meet the economic criteria for EMU are committed to joining the single currency.
The only exceptions are Denmark, which has already decided not to join, and Britain, which negotiated the right to opt out of monetary union.
Sweden has repeatedly said its national parliament will decide whether the country joins or not but it does not have the same kind of formal possibility to stay out as Denmark and Britain have.
